source.paper: Arkani-Hamed, Figueiredo, Hall, Manzari — The Very Nearly Right Theory of Flavor
source.note: Example I of App. III; the pi/2 texture of Fig. 2 (class 4).

parameters.coefficient_convention: all u_ij, d_ij real positive O(1); single phase e^{i phi} on one loop edge

phi.placement_note: paper's Fig. 2 places the phase on Y^d_22; Eq. S38 realizes it as i*u12 on Y^u_12 instead — same loop, phase moved by rephasing, consistent with the placement-convention freedom of App. V.a footnote 7

loop.convention: a link is conjugated if its arrow points towards a q node (App. V.a)

perfect_matchings.note: matchings are enumerated by the checker from the actual matrices; recorded here are the expectations
perfect_matchings.paper_eq_8_discrepancy: The paper's Eq. 8 (det Yu = Yu_11 Yu_22 Yu_33, det Yd = Yd_12 Yd_21 Yd_33) belongs to the Fig. 2 presentation, whose Yu edge set must contain (1,1) and whose matching is diagonal. That presentation is NOT a row/column permutation of the S38 pair used in App. III Example I: S38 Yu has row-degree sequence (1,2,1) while the Fig. 2 Yu implied by Eq. 8 has (2,1,1), and no combined row/column permutation maps the S38 pair to it. The two presentations share the loop monomial Yu_12 Yu_22* Yd_22 Yd_12* but are distinct texture charts (possibly distinct pi/2 classes). The checker therefore works strictly from Eq. S38's matrices and treats Fig. 2/Eq. 8 as a separate chart whose exact edge set is only partially recoverable from the text extraction.

strong_cp_feature.as_written_S38_phase_on_Yu12: phase edge Yu_12 BELONGS to the unique Yu matching, so arg det(YuYd) = pi/2 as written
strong_cp_feature.after_rephasing: the loop edges Yu_22 and Yd_22 belong to no determinant matching; moving the phase there by node rephasing gives arg det(YuYd) = 0 (paper: phase placement within the loop is a rephasing choice)
strong_cp_feature.scope: graph-combinatorial determinant reality only; not a complete strong-CP solution
